newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian dollar ends stronger on IMM and crosses.
newsitem.headline: Canadian dollar ends stronger on IMM and crosses.

text.p: * The Canadian dollar ended trade on Wednesday stronger at C$1.3625 (US$0.7339) from this morning's open of C$1.3671 (US$0.7314) on corporate buying interest, dealers said. * They said interest to buy the Canada around the C$1.3700 level emerged from Chicago's International Monetary Market and on the crosses against the Australian dollar.
"I think Chicago was there buying and I think the Canada also benefitted from some Aussie trading," the trader said.
He said the straight cross-trading of Australian dollars for Canada added to the strength along with stop-loss buying, which emerged as the U.S. dollar weakened.

On the crosses, Canada's dollar strengthened to A$0.9221 from Tuesday's close of A$0.9216 and also firmed in Asia against the yen to 89.62 yen from 89.07 yen. The Canadian dollar slipped some against the mark however, to 1.2414 marks from 1.2467 marks. Traders said a weaker U.S. dollar produced some stop-loss buying of Canada.

The U.S. dollar slid against the mark and yen on Wednesday after the Federal Reserve's Beige Book reported the U.S. economy continues to expand at a "relatively moderate pace" with temperate price pressures.
